A method for manufacturing the composition begins with a raw material composition that contains at least one polyunsaturated fatty acid having 20 or more carbon atoms. The raw material composition is subjected to hydrolysis using a reaction solution that includes the raw material composition, a lower alcohol, ultra-low-metal water, and an alkali catalyst.

After the hydrolysis step, contact between the resulting composition and metal is carefully limited. Specifically, the contact is controlled so that the product of the metal contact surface area per gram of the composition and the contact time is 100 or less. outputs.L4:
A free-polyunsaturated-fatty-acid composition and a method for manufacturing the same are provided. The composition is obtained by hydrolyzing a raw material that contains long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, particularly polyunsaturated fatty acids having 20 or more carbon atoms, under conditions that suppress metal contamination. In the manufacturing process, the raw material is treated with water having a low metal content, a lower alcohol, and an alkali catalyst to promote hydrolysis and convert fatty-acid esters into free fatty acids. After the hydrolysis reaction, contact between the reaction product and metal-containing equipment, materials, or processing aids is restricted as much as possible so that the final product retains a very low metal concentration.

The resulting composition contains fatty acids in which at least 80.0% by mass are free polyunsaturated fatty acids having 20 or more carbon atoms. Examples of such long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids may include eicosapentaenoic acid, docosahexaenoic acid, arachidonic acid, and other highly unsaturated fatty acids derived from natural oils or other lipid-containing raw materials. Because the process uses low-metal water and limits exposure to metal sources after hydrolysis, the total metal content of the composition is controlled to 0.1 ppm or less.

This low-metal, high-purity free-polyunsaturated-fatty-acid composition is advantageous because metals can promote oxidation, discoloration, odor formation, and degradation of polyunsaturated fatty acids. By reducing metal contamination to an extremely low level, the composition has improved stability, purity, and quality. The method is therefore useful for producing free long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids suitable for applications requiring strict control of impurities, such as nutritional products, pharmaceutical preparations, functional foods, supplements, cosmetics, and other high-grade lipid materials.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent claim-style summary for an invention involving a free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition with very low metal content and a manufacturing method using hydrolysis, low-metal water, lower alcohol, and alkali catalyst.
counterfactuals.output:
### Patent Claim-Style Summary

1. **A free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition**, comprising one or more free polyunsaturated fatty acids, wherein the composition has a total metal content of not more than about 10 ppm, and wherein the one or more free polyunsaturated fatty acids comprise at least one omega-3, omega-6, or omega-9 polyunsaturated fatty acid.

2. The composition of claim 1, wherein the total metal content is not more than about 5 ppm, preferably not more than about 1 ppm.

3. The composition of claim 1 or 2, wherein the metal content comprises one or more of sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, iron, copper, nickel, chromium, zinc, aluminum, or tin.

4. The composition of any preceding claim, wherein the free polyunsaturated fatty acid comprises eicosapentaenoic acid, docosahexaenoic acid, alpha-linolenic acid, gamma-linolenic acid, arachidonic acid, or a combination thereof.

5. The composition of any preceding claim, wherein the composition is substantially free of fatty acid metal salts.

6. The composition of any preceding claim, wherein the composition has improved oxidative stability relative to a corresponding free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition having a higher metal content.

7. **A method of manufacturing a low-metal free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition**, comprising:  
   (a) providing a lipid starting material comprising one or more esterified polyunsaturated fatty acids;  
   (b) contacting the lipid starting material with a reaction medium comprising low-metal water, a lower alcohol, and an alkali catalyst under hydrolysis conditions to form a hydrolyzed reaction mixture comprising free polyunsaturated fatty acids or salts thereof;  
   (c) acidifying the hydrolyzed reaction mixture to convert fatty acid salts to free fatty acids; and  
   (d) recovering a free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition having a total metal content of not more than about 10 ppm.

8. The method of claim 7, wherein the low-metal water has a total metal content of not more than about 1 ppm.

9. The method of claim 7 or 8, wherein the lower alcohol comprises methanol, ethanol, propanol, isopropanol, butanol, or a mixture thereof.

10. The method of any of claims 7–9, wherein the alkali catalyst comprises an alkali metal hydroxide, alkali metal alkoxide, alkali metal carbonate, or a combination thereof.

11. The method of any of claims 7–10, wherein the alkali catalyst comprises sodium hydroxide, potassium hydroxide, sodium methoxide, potassium methoxide, sodium ethoxide, potassium ethoxide, or a combination thereof.

12. The method of any of claims 7–11, further comprising washing the recovered free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition with low-metal water to reduce residual metal content.

13. The method of any of claims 7–12, further comprising separating an alcohol-containing phase from a fatty acid-containing phase.

14. The method of any of claims 7–13, further comprising subjecting the recovered free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition to purification by distillation, chromatography, extraction, crystallization, membrane separation, or a combination thereof.

15. The method of any of claims 7–14, wherein the lipid starting material comprises fish oil, algal oil, microbial oil, plant oil, krill oil, marine oil, or a concentrate thereof.

16. The method of any of claims 7–15, wherein the hydrolysis conditions include a temperature of about 20°C to about 100°C.

17. The method of any of claims 7–16, wherein the hydrolysis is performed under an inert atmosphere.

18. The method of any of claims 7–17, wherein the recovered free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition comprises at least about 50 wt.% total free polyunsaturated fatty acids.

19. The method of any of claims 7–18, wherein the recovered composition has a sodium and potassium content, individually or collectively, of not more than about 5 ppm.

20. **A low-metal free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition produced by the method of any of claims 7–19.**
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention in one paragraph: a composition containing at least 80% free long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids with total metal content of 0.1 ppm or less, plus a process that controls post-hydrolysis metal contact.
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a highly purified fatty acid composition and a method for producing it, in which the composition contains at least 80% by weight free long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, such as omega-3 fatty acids, and has an exceptionally low total metal content of 0.1 ppm or less. The process includes hydrolyzing a lipid feedstock to release the free fatty acids, followed by purification and handling steps designed to minimize or prevent metal contamination after hydrolysis, for example by using non-metallic, passivated, or otherwise inert contact surfaces and carefully controlled processing, storage, and transfer conditions. By limiting post-hydrolysis contact with metal-containing equipment or materials, the method reduces metal-catalyzed oxidation and degradation, thereby improving the stability, purity, and suitability of the long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid composition for nutritional, pharmaceutical, or other high-value applications.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise patent abstract for a free-PUFA-containing composition and its preparation method, specifying C20+ fatty acids, low metal content, hydrolysis conditions, and a limit on metal contact expressed as T ≤ 100 cm²×days.
counterfactuals.output: A composition comprising free polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) is provided, wherein at least 50 wt% of the fatty acids are C20 or higher PUFAs, including one or more of eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), and docosapentaenoic acid (DPA), and wherein the composition has a total transition metal content of less than 5 ppm. The composition is prepared by hydrolyzing a PUFA-containing lipid feedstock under aqueous, enzymatic or alkaline hydrolysis conditions at about 20–90°C, followed by acidification and recovery of the free fatty acid fraction. During preparation and storage, contact with metal surfaces is limited such that T, defined as the product of exposed metal surface area in cm² and contact time in days per kg of composition, is T ≤ 100 cm²×days, thereby reducing oxidation and improving stability of the free-PUFA composition.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a claim-like technical disclosure for manufacturing a purified free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition from a raw material using lower alcohol, ultrapure water, and an alkali catalyst, while minimizing contamination from metal surfaces.
counterfactuals.output:
1. A method for manufacturing a purified free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition, the method comprising:

   (a) providing a lipid-containing raw material comprising one or more polyunsaturated fatty acid residues;

   (b) contacting the lipid-containing raw material with a lower alcohol, ultrapure water, and an alkali catalyst under reaction conditions sufficient to convert at least a portion of the lipid-containing raw material into an alkali salt of a fatty acid and/or a lower-alkyl ester intermediate;

   (c) converting the alkali salt and/or lower-alkyl ester intermediate to a free fatty acid-containing mixture comprising at least one free polyunsaturated fatty acid;

   (d) separating and purifying the free fatty acid-containing mixture to obtain a purified free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition; and

   (e) conducting at least steps (b) through (d) in equipment configured such that contact between the reaction mixture, intermediate mixture, or purified free fatty acid composition and exposed metal surfaces is minimized.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the lower alcohol comprises methanol, ethanol, propanol, isopropanol, butanol, or a mixture thereof.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the lower alcohol comprises ethanol.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein the ultrapure water has a resistivity of at least 10 MΩ·cm, at least 15 MΩ·cm, or at least 18 MΩ·cm at 25°C.

5. The method of claim 1, wherein the alkali catalyst comprises sodium hydroxide, potassium hydroxide, sodium methoxide, potassium methoxide, sodium ethoxide, potassium ethoxide, sodium carbonate, potassium carbonate, or a mixture thereof.

6. The method of claim 1, wherein the lipid-containing raw material comprises fish oil, krill oil, algal oil, microbial oil, plant oil, marine oil, a refined triglyceride oil, a phospholipid-containing oil, an ethyl ester concentrate, or a mixture thereof.

7. The method of claim 1, wherein the polyunsaturated fatty acid comprises an omega-3 fatty acid.

8. The method of claim 7, wherein the omega-3 fatty acid comprises eicosapentaenoic acid, docosahexaenoic acid, docosapentaenoic acid, or a mixture thereof.

9. The method of claim 1, wherein converting the alkali salt and/or lower-alkyl ester intermediate to the free fatty acid-containing mixture comprises acidifying with an acid to a pH sufficient to liberate free fatty acids.

10. The method of claim 9, wherein the acid comprises hydrochloric acid, sulfuric acid, phosphoric acid, citric acid, acetic acid, or a mixture thereof.

11. The method of claim 1, wherein purifying comprises one or more of liquid-liquid extraction, washing, evaporation, distillation, molecular distillation, short-path distillation, chromatography, winterization, crystallization, urea complexation, membrane separation, deodorization, or filtration.

12. The method of claim 1, wherein the purified free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition comprises at least 50 wt%, at least 70 wt%, at least 80 wt%, at least 90 wt%, or at least 95 wt% total free polyunsaturated fatty acids based on total fatty acids.

13. The method of claim 1, wherein the purified free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition comprises free eicosapentaenoic acid and/or free docosahexaenoic acid.

14. The method of claim 1, wherein the equipment comprises contact surfaces formed from glass, glass-lined metal, fluoropolymer, perfluoroalkoxy polymer, polytetrafluoroethylene, polypropylene, polyethylene, polyether ether ketone, ceramic, enamel, or another non-metallic or passivated material.

15. The method of claim 1, wherein metal-contact minimization comprises using one or more of a glass-lined reactor, a polymer-lined transfer line, a non-metallic pump head, a non-metallic valve, a ceramic filter housing, a fluoropolymer gasket, a fluoropolymer-lined vessel, or a passivated stainless-steel component having a protective inert coating.

16. The method of claim 1, wherein no uncoated stainless steel, carbon steel, copper, brass, bronze, aluminum, nickel, or iron-containing surface directly contacts the reaction mixture, intermediate mixture, or purified free fatty acid composition after formation of the free fatty acid-containing mixture.

17. The method of claim 1, wherein the purified free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition has a metal impurity content of less than 1 ppm total iron, copper, nickel, chromium, aluminum, and manganese.

18. The method of claim 1, wherein the purified free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition has an iron content of less than 0.5 ppm and a copper content of less than 0.1 ppm.

19. The method of claim 1, wherein oxygen exposure is reduced during at least one of reacting, converting, separating, purifying, or storing by use of nitrogen, argon, vacuum, degassed solvent, or an oxygen-impermeable vessel.

20. The method of claim 1, wherein an antioxidant is added before, during, or after purification, the antioxidant comprising tocopherol, ascorbyl palmitate, rosemary extract, citric acid, lecithin, butylated hydroxytoluene, butylated hydroxyanisole, tert-butylhydroquinone, or a mixture thereof.

21. The method of claim 1, wherein the lower alcohol and ultrapure water are pretreated to reduce dissolved metal content before contacting the lipid-containing raw material.

22. The method of claim 1, wherein the lower alcohol and ultrapure water are passed through an ion-exchange resin, chelating resin, sub-micron filter, activated carbon, or a combination thereof before use.

23. The method of claim 1, wherein the method further comprises washing the free fatty acid-containing mixture with ultrapure water to remove residual alkali catalyst, alcohol, salts, soap, glycerol, or hydrophilic impurities.

24. The method of claim 1, wherein the purified free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition is collected, transferred, and stored in a container having a product-contact surface comprising glass, fluoropolymer, polymer-lined metal, ceramic, or a coated metal surface.

25. A purified free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition produced by the method of any one of claims 1-24, wherein the composition comprises a reduced concentration of metal contaminants relative to a corresponding composition manufactured in equipment having exposed metal product-contact surfaces.

26. A manufacturing system for producing a purified free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition, the system comprising:

   (a) a reaction vessel configured to receive a lipid-containing raw material, a lower alcohol, ultrapure water, and an alkali catalyst;

   (b) an acidification vessel or conversion zone configured to form free fatty acids;

   (c) a purification unit configured to enrich one or more free polyunsaturated fatty acids; and

   (d) transfer lines, pumps, valves, filters, seals, and storage vessels arranged such that product-contact surfaces are non-metallic, lined, coated, glass-lined, ceramic, fluoropolymer-based, polymer-based, or otherwise configured to reduce metal contamination of the free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition.

27. The system of claim 26, wherein the purification unit comprises a short-path distillation unit, molecular distillation unit, chromatography unit, extraction unit, crystallization unit, membrane unit, filtration unit, or a combination thereof.

28. The system of claim 26, wherein the product-contact surfaces are selected to limit leaching of iron, copper, nickel, chromium, aluminum, or manganese into the free polyunsaturated fatty acid composition.

29. A technical process for reducing metal contamination during manufacture of a free omega-3 fatty acid composition, comprising carrying out alkali-catalyzed alcoholysis and/or hydrolysis of an omega-3-containing oil using a lower alcohol and ultrapure water, liberating free omega-3 fatty acids by acidification, purifying the liberated free omega-3 fatty acids, and preventing direct contact of the liberated free omega-3 fatty acids with exposed metal surfaces during purification and collection.

30. The process of claim 29, wherein the free omega-3 fatty acid composition comprises free EPA, free DHA, or a mixture thereof, and contains less than 1 ppm total transition metals.
